newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Downtrend stalls in U.S. debt futures.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Downtrend stalls in U.S. debt futures.

text.p: While bond bears haven't thrown in the towel yet, Friday's low of 106-23 in June futures is starting to look like a bottom to some technicians.

Following a restrained sell-off on as-expected March employment data, June bond futures have spent the past two sessions consolidating within Friday's parameters. The contract skidded to its lowest level in seven months after the report.
"We've probably seen the low and will spend some time this week building a base," said Jim Bohan, senior financial futures strategist at Merrill Lynch Capital Markets.

"The employment number turned everbody bearish," he noted, yet the market did not break down completely on the data and is very oversold. "I think that suggests we're going to be turning up from here," Bohan said.
Other bond analysts argue it's hard to fight a trend and want to see more evidence that downside momentum has dried up.
"I think the decline that started on Feb. 18 has not yet completed," said Joe Plauche, financial futures analyst for Dean Witter. "The bear trend is intact."

Today's high of 107-24 in June bonds could be the extent of the latest bear market correction, Plauche said. He projects more declines to 106-08 later this week or early next week, as the yield on the benchmark 30-year bond flirts with 7.20 percent, then a rebound possibly to 108-00.
"But the bigger trend is still down," he emphasized.
June bond futures recently were trading at 107-11, down 9/32.
Bohan said if 106-23 proves to be a near-term bottom, the June contract has the potential to reach the 109-00 to 110-00 area in the next couple of weeks.
Bolstering the case for a bottom in the debt market, he said, is the recent pattern in September Eurodollars, which put in a low at 93.63 six days ago.

Analysts said Eurodollar prices already reflect one or two more rate tightenings, leaving little leeway to trade lower. Bohan's upside target for September Euros is 93.90 to 93.94. The contract was last trading down two basis points at 93.715.
"The market's in a good position to respond to any positive news," Bohan said.
